text: Privacy Policy
Last updated: 27 September 2026
At Elevate Core, privacy is part of how we build trust with candidates, clients, partners and people who visit our website.

This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, store and protect personal data, as well as the rights available to you under the General Data Protection Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (“GDPR”) and other applicable data protection laws.
1. Who we are
Elevate Core is a recruiting partner working with businesses and professionals across Ukraine and Europe.
For the purposes of the GDPR, the data controller is:

ElevateCoreOutsourcing, obrt za poslovno savjetovanje i usluge Owner: Tetiana Borysova Registered office: Banski Vinogradi 44A, 10000 Zagreb, Croatia OIB / VAT ID: HR88011431269 Registration No.: 99044129 Trading as: Elevate Core Email: hello@el-core.eu Website: https://el-core.eu
For privacy-related questions or requests, please contact us at hello@el-core.eu.
2. Who this Policy applies to
This Privacy Policy applies to personal data relating to:
candidates and potential candidates;
people who contact us regarding career opportunities;
client representatives and prospective clients;
business partners, suppliers and professional contacts;
people who communicate with us through our website, email, LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Telegram or other channels;
visitors to our website.
3. Personal data we may collect
Depending on how you interact with Elevate Core, we may process the following categories of personal data.
Candidates and potential candidates
This may include:
name and contact details;
location and preferred work location;
CV, résumé or professional profile;
employment history;
education and qualifications;
professional skills and experience;
languages;
current or expected compensation, where relevant;
job preferences and availability;
links to professional profiles, portfolios or publicly available work;
information shared during calls, interviews or correspondence;
interview and assessment notes;
information relating to recruitment processes and applications;
references, where appropriate;
other information you voluntarily provide to us.

We do not intentionally request special categories of personal data, such as information about health, ethnicity, religion, political opinions, sexual orientation or similar sensitive information, unless this is necessary and legally permitted.
Please avoid including unnecessary sensitive personal information in your CV or communications.
Clients, partners and business contacts
We may process:
name;
job title and company;
business email and telephone number;
information about your organisation;
correspondence and meeting information;
information relating to recruitment projects, contracts and services;
billing and administrative information where applicable.
Website visitors
Depending on the configuration of our website, we may collect:
IP address;
device and browser information;
website usage information;
approximate location derived from technical information;
cookie and consent preferences;
information submitted through website forms.
4. Where we obtain personal data
We may receive personal data directly from you when you:
contact us;
submit a CV or professional profile;
apply for or discuss an opportunity;
book a call;
communicate with us through email or messaging platforms;
enter into a business relationship with us.
Because recruitment often involves proactive search, we may also obtain professional information from other lawful sources, including:
LinkedIn and other professional networks;
job boards and recruitment platforms;
publicly available professional websites;
company websites;
professional communities;
referrals and recommendations;
our clients or business partners;
previous professional communications with you.

Where we obtain your personal data from another source and Article 14 GDPR applies, we will provide the required information within the period required by law — generally no later than one month after obtaining the data, at the time of our first communication with you, or before the first disclosure of your data to another recipient, as applicable.
5. Why we process personal data
Recruitment and candidate search
We may process personal data to:
identify professionals who may be relevant to current or future opportunities;
assess professional background and potential fit;
contact candidates regarding relevant opportunities;
manage recruitment and interview processes;
communicate with candidates;
present relevant candidate profiles to clients;
maintain appropriate records of recruitment activity;
consider candidates for future opportunities.

We do not send a candidate’s profile to a client for a specific recruitment process without informing the candidate about the opportunity and intended disclosure, unless another lawful basis and exceptional circumstances apply.
Client and business relationships
We may process personal data to:
respond to enquiries;
understand business and hiring needs;
prepare proposals;
provide recruitment and related services;
manage contracts and projects;
communicate with client teams;
maintain business records;
manage billing and legal obligations.
Website operation and security
We may process data to:
operate and secure our website;
prevent fraud, misuse or technical attacks;
understand how the website performs;
remember privacy and cookie preferences.
Marketing and professional communication
Where permitted, we may contact existing or prospective business contacts about Elevate Core services, insights or relevant professional information.
Where consent is legally required, we will only send such communications after obtaining consent.
You can unsubscribe or object to direct marketing at any time.
6. Legal bases for processing
Depending on the circumstances, we process personal data on one or more of the following legal bases under Article 6 GDPR:

Legitimate interests — for example, identifying and contacting professionals regarding relevant career opportunities, developing business relationships, providing recruitment services, improving our services and protecting our systems.
When relying on legitimate interests, we consider whether our interests are proportionate and whether your rights and reasonable expectations override those interests.
Performance of a contract or steps before entering into a contract — for example, when providing services to a client or responding to a request to enter into a contractual relationship.
Consent — where you have specifically agreed to particular processing, including certain marketing communications or non-essential cookies.
You may withdraw consent at any time. Withdrawal does not affect processing that took place lawfully before the withdrawal.
Legal obligation — where processing is necessary to comply with accounting, tax, regulatory, legal or other statutory requirements.
Establishment, exercise or defence of legal claims — where necessary to protect our legal rights.
7. Sharing personal data
We do not sell personal data.
We may share personal data only where necessary and appropriate with:
Elevate Core team members involved in the relevant work;
clients for whom we conduct recruitment assignments;
technology providers supporting our business, such as hosting, cloud storage, email, CRM or applicant tracking systems;
communication and scheduling providers;
professional advisers, including accountants and legal advisers;
regulators, courts or public authorities where legally required;
other service providers acting on our behalf.

Service providers processing personal data on our behalf are required to protect that information and process it only under appropriate contractual and legal safeguards. When a candidate profile is shared with a client, the client may become an independent data controller for its subsequent recruitment process and may provide its own privacy information.
8. LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Telegram and other external platforms
Our website may contain links to or allow communication through third-party services such as LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Telegram or scheduling platforms.
When you use these services, the relevant provider may process personal data independently under its own privacy terms.
We recommend reviewing the privacy policies of those services.
9. International data transfers
We work internationally and may use service providers or work with clients located both inside and outside the European Economic Area (“EEA”).
As a result, personal data may sometimes be transferred outside the EEA.
Where GDPR rules on international transfers apply, we use an appropriate transfer mechanism permitted under Chapter V GDPR, such as:
a European Commission adequacy decision;
Standard Contractual Clauses approved by the European Commission, where applicable;
another legally recognised safeguard or derogation where appropriate.
Where required, we also assess whether additional safeguards are necessary to provide an appropriate level of protection.
10. How long we keep personal data
We retain personal data only for as long as reasonably necessary for the purpose for which it was collected, taking into account legal, contractual and operational requirements.
As a general guideline:
candidate and professional profile data may be retained for up to 24 months after our last meaningful interaction;
information relating to active recruitment processes may be retained during the recruitment process and for up to 24 months afterwards;
general enquiries may be retained for up to 24 months after the last communication;
client and business contact information may generally be retained for up to 3 years after the last meaningful business interaction;
contractual, accounting and financial records are retained for the period required by applicable law;
marketing information is retained until you unsubscribe, object, or the information is no longer relevant;
technical and security logs may be retained for a limited period where necessary for security and system integrity.
We may retain information for longer where necessary to comply with legal obligations, resolve disputes or establish, exercise or defend legal claims.
You may ask us to delete your data earlier where the GDPR gives you that right.
11. Your data protection rights
Subject to the GDPR and any applicable limitations, you may have the right to:
access your personal data;
correct inaccurate or incomplete personal data;
request deletion of your personal data;
request restriction of processing;
object to processing based on legitimate interests;
object at any time to direct marketing;
receive certain personal data in a structured, commonly used and machine-readable format and request data portability;
withdraw consent where processing is based on consent;
lodge a complaint with a supervisory authority;
receive information about applicable safeguards for international transfers;
not be subject to certain decisions based solely on automated processing where Article 22 GDPR applies.
To exercise your rights, contact us at hello@el-core.eu.
We may need to verify your identity before responding to a request.
We normally respond within the time limits required by applicable data protection law.
12. Automated decision-making

Elevate Core does not currently make recruitment decisions that produce legal or similarly significant effects on individuals solely through automated processing. Technology may be used to support organisation, search, analysis or recruitment workflows, but relevant recruitment decisions involve human assessment.
If this changes, we will provide the information required by applicable law.
13. Cookies and similar technologies
Our website may use cookies and similar technologies.
Cookies that are strictly necessary for the operation, security or functionality of the website may be used where legally permitted without consent.
Analytics, advertising, personalisation or other non-essential technologies will only be activated where the legally required consent has been obtained.
Where consent is required, you can:
accept or reject non-essential cookies;
choose between available categories;
change or withdraw your choices later.
More detailed information about individual cookies, their providers, purposes and duration should be available in our Cookie Policy / Cookie Settings.
Withdrawing consent will not affect the lawfulness of processing carried out before withdrawal.
14. Data security
We use appropriate technical and organisational measures designed to protect personal data against:
unauthorised access;
accidental loss;
alteration;
disclosure;
destruction;
misuse.
Access to personal data is limited to people and providers who need it for legitimate business purposes.
No internet-based system can provide absolute security, but we regularly review our safeguards in light of the nature and risks of the processing.
15. Third-party websites
Our website may contain links to external websites.
Elevate Core is not responsible for the privacy practices of third-party websites or services. Their processing of personal data is governed by their own privacy policies.
16. Complaints
If you have concerns about how we process your personal data, we encourage you to contact us first at:
hello@el-core.eu
You also have the right to lodge a complaint with the data protection authority in the EU/EEA Member State of your habitual residence, place of work or the place of the alleged infringement.
Where the competent Croatian authority is applicable:
Croatian Personal Data Protection Agency (AZOP) Agencija za zaštitu osobnih podataka Selska cesta 136 10000 Zagreb Croatia Email: azop@azop.hr
17. Changes to this Privacy Policy
We may update this Privacy Policy when our services, technologies, legal obligations or data-processing practices change.
The latest version will always be published on this page together with the date of the most recent update.
18. Contact us
For questions about this Privacy Policy, our use of personal data, or to exercise your data protection rights, contact:
